results.title: HOW TO | Connect Playback to a Dante Network
results.summary: Playback can use a Dante network as its audio device over a single Ethernet cable instead of an interface and DI boxes. Two documented options. Option 1, Mac only: Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS, up to 32 outputs, one-time license from Audinate), with the Mac on the Dante network by Cat-6 to a shared switch or router, using a USB-to-Ethernet adapter if the Mac has no Ethernet port; selected in Playback via Settings > General > Audio Device once DVS is running. Option 2, iOS and Mac: a Dante AVIO USB adapter (a USB dongle with an Ethernet port) limited to 2 outputs, output 1 click/guide and output 2 tracks; this is the ONLY documented way to put an iPad or iPhone on a Dante network. The article states Playback does NOT support Dante Via, and warns that not all USB Ethernet adapters work reliably, pointing to Audinate's adapter recommendations for macOS. SoundGrid is not covered here.

steps.text: Confirm the platform first: DVS is Mac only; an iPad or iPhone can only join a Dante network through a Dante AVIO USB adapter (2 outputs). A plain USB-to-Ethernet adapter on an iPad is not a documented Dante setup.
DVS (Mac): install Playback, then download Dante Virtual Soundcard and buy the one-time license from Audinate. Playback does not support Dante Via.
DVS (Mac): connect the Mac to the same wired network as the Dante devices with a Cat-6 cable to a shared switch or router. Dante needs a hard-wired connection, not Wi-Fi.

DVS (Mac): if the Mac has no built-in Ethernet port, use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter. The article warns not all adapters work reliably and links Audinate's FAQ 'DVS: USB Ethernet Adaptor Choice for macOS Systems' (https://www.audinate.com/learning/faqs/dvs-usb-ethernet-adaptor-choice-for-macos-systems), which recommends adapters that use the USB CDC-NCM driver standard and notes many common 1 Gbps adapters (Realtek RTL8153 chip) only support CDC-ECM.

DVS (Mac): in the DVS app choose the channel count (16x16 or 32x32 recommended), select the network interface the Dante network is on (a valid choice shows an IP address), then press Start. DVS must be running before it can appear as an audio device.

DVS (Mac): in Playback go to Settings > General, click the Audio Device cell, and choose Dante Virtual Soundcard. This also makes Dante the computer's audio device, so turn on Do Not Disturb to keep system sounds out of the track outputs.

DVS (Mac): route Playback buses to the outputs you want (the output count matches the DVS configuration, e.g. 16x16 gives 16), then patch Playback's outputs to destination devices in Dante Controller.

AVIO adapter (iOS and Mac): connect the Dante AVIO USB adapter between the device and the Dante network; it provides 2 outputs (output 1 click/guide, output 2 tracks). The article gives no further steps for this option. The supported-devices list marks the AVIO adapter as 'setup required'.

results.title: Playback Subscriptions | Explained
results.summary: Separates Playback Features (Intro, Premium, Cloud Pro, Live Bundle), Playback Content (Rentals, purchased tracks, Sounds, uploaded Cloud Songs, click and guide), and Playback Access (Team Sharing seats). Playback Intro is free on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS but limited to a single stereo output and excludes Premium features (editing arrangements, Playback Remote, Playback Sync). Cloud Pro adds click and guide for every song, Team Sharing seats, and saved custom-named arrangements; uploading Cloud Songs requires Cloud Pro. Rentals are device-specific and not shared. The article does not explain how to check or manage the subscription in-app.

results.title: Playback FAQs
results.summary: The help center's Playback FAQ article has two questions. (1) How do I get song content for Playback: five documented ways: Playback Rentals (recommended, cheapest for weekly use), purchasing Artist Original Master Track products on MultiTracks.com (buy once, stays available for your location; extra licenses for additional campuses), uploading your own content with Cloud Pro (multitracks or single-file backing tracks, then add click, guide and song sections), using just the Click & Guide for any catalog song (requires Cloud Pro, Live Bundle, or Playback Rentals), and Sounds content (ambient pads and Soundbeds purchased on MultiTracks.com appear in Playback for free). (2) Does Playback show lyrics or chords: No. Playback is audio-first and does not display lyrics or charts.

steps.text: To get songs: unlock a Playback Rental, buy the track product on MultiTracks.com, upload your own content with Cloud Pro, use Click & Guide only (Cloud Pro, Live Bundle, or Rentals), or use purchased Sounds pads and Soundbeds.
Playback does not display lyrics or chord charts; it is audio-first. (ChartBuilder is MultiTracks' charts product; charts are out of Playback support scope.)

results.title: Managing ChartBuilder and Playback Devices
results.summary: Each Playback user may be signed in on two devices; a user with a Playback Premium seat gets three. Devices are viewed and removed from the Playback Devices section of the user's account page on MultiTracks.com. TestFlight/beta builds register as separate devices.

steps.text: View or manage Playback devices: 'Playback Devices' section of your user-account page, or https://www.multitracks.com/premium/playback/devices.aspx
Remove a device: on the Devices page under your username account page, click the 'X' next to the device. This signs that user out of the device and frees a slot.
Add a device: confirm an 'Available device' is listed, then sign in to Playback with the user's credentials.
Beta/TestFlight builds typically register as separate devices even on the same hardware, so running both can reach the limit faster.
To give more people access, add them as users and grant seats and setlist access; the per-user limit itself cannot be raised except via the Premium seat.

results.title: Playback Download Error (Download Unauthorized)
results.summary: Explains the message 'There was an error while authorizing the download of [song]', which means the download URL has expired or is unauthorized on the current network. Listed causes are a VPN on the Playback device, network administrator settings (multiple WAN uplinks, blocked domains or ports), or the network/IP address changing mid-download. The fix is to retry on a different connection or change the network's settings, ideally with a network admin or ISP.

steps.text: iCloud Private Relay (Apple): set the 'IP Address Location' option to 'Use Country & Time Zone'. The article warns that 'Maintain General Location' can cause this error.
Turn off any VPN or VPN software on the device. Examples named in the article: Accountable2You, CovenantEyes, NordVPN, Surfshark.
Try downloading on a different internet network from a different provider.

Advanced (IT/network admin) - multiple WAN uplinks: the download request may leave through one uplink while the content download tries another. Pin requests to a specific WAN uplink in the advanced traffic network preferences, or adjust the WAN uplink settings. Contact support for help pinning requests.

Advanced - other network settings: MultiTracks.com sends all traffic over port 443 (SSL); make sure it is not blocked. A static IP is not required, but if a download request uses a specific IP address, the same IP must complete the download.
Still stuck: use the messenger in the bottom right of MultiTracks.com or email Support@MultiTracks.com.

results.title: Playback General Settings Overview
results.summary: Lists every setting in the General tab (three-line menu icon top-right > General). Audio-relevant items: Auto-Pan, Click Sound, Song Specific Buses (Premium), Audio Device (shows and sets which connected device Playback uses for all audio output), Power Saver, MIDI Out, and SMPTE Timecode. The page gives no detail on Audio Device choices and does not mention sample rate, Bluetooth, storage, or subscription display.

steps.text: Open settings: tap the three-line menu icon in the top-right corner of Playback and make sure the General tab is selected.
Audio Device: shows and sets which connected audio device Playback uses for all audio output.
Auto-Pan: routes click and guide to the left mono output and all tracks to the right mono output of the device's stereo output.
Song Specific Buses (Premium): on gives each song its own bus fader mix; off uses one global bus mix.
Power Saver: improves performance on older devices; disables fader VU meters and fader multi-touch and reduces waveform scrolling feedback.
MIDI Out: enabled by default; disable if unused to improve performance and battery life.
SMPTE Timecode: toggles SMPTE output and selects frame rate.
Fader Default Level at 80%: on presets faders to 80% for headroom; off loads tracks at 100%.

results.text:
When opening Playback for the first time, the login screen will appear. In order to log into Playback, a MultiTracks.com account is required. From this screen, you have two options:

1. Sign up for a free MultiTracks.com account. The first admin MultiTracks.com account is the first step towards building your MultiTracks.com organization, but does not require payment info. This lets you explore Playback’s menus and free features without paid content.
2. Log into your MultiTracks.com user account, created on the web.
